target_customer: Consumers with wavy, curly and kinky-coily hair buying online, with salons as a planned wholesale channel
problem: People with curly hair struggle to find simple, suitable products and often feel pushed to mask their natural features.
business_model: Direct to consumer e-commerce of hair care products with high gross margin
product_category: Beauty and hair care brand (Love Ur Curls)

founders.name: Sahar Saidi
education: Dropped out of college at first, then double MBA 2015 from University of Toronto and University of St. Gallen

competitors.name: Function of Beauty
competitors.what: Customized shampoo and conditioner direct to consumer, another YC beauty company
competitors.funding_then: Series A $9.5M led by GGV in March 2017 per CB Insights style listings (not opened)

technical_complexity.rationale: Formulating and selling hair products through contract manufacturing and a Shopify style store; main hard parts were inventory and customer service.

defensibility.rationale: Hair care is crowded with established lines; edge came from simple three step routines, one to one customer support and community.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large groups bought or launched textured hair lines over the following years (secondary market report); DevaCurl was bought by Henkel in 2019. No evidence they targeted LUS.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported more than $1M in sales in its first year with over 80 percent gross margins and stockouts that forced preorders.

branding.name_origin: LUS stands for Love Ur Self, tied to the founder's story of low self-esteem as a child.
branding.domain_note: lusbrands.com now redirects to loveurcurls.com (site fetch, 2026)

identity.voice_and_tone: Self love and confidence messaging, non beauty beauty brand

branding.brand_signature: Love Ur Curls three step routine chosen by hair type

rebrands.why: Company says curl type was never the full story (June 2026 press release); product name stays

branding.community_and_virality: Founder cites 500,000 plus customers in 2020 and the company claims 2 million households by 2026; one to one social media support credited for growth.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional (Canada) brand with real community and press, founder profiled by Toronto outlets, but no evidence of iconic status.

outcome_analysis: LUS Brands launched as a self funded direct to consumer curly hair brand and passed one million dollars in first year sales before going through YC Winter 2018. It remains active under the Love Ur Curls name, reporting millions of households served in 2026, so it looks like a durable niche consumer brand that grew mostly on margin and community rather than large venture rounds.
notes: Funding is only in aggregators and conflicts: CB Insights $120K seed 2018-03-14, Preqin about $1.1M with Comcast Ventures; investor lists vary (Willow Growth Partners, CV Catalyst, Duro Ventures, Sound Ventures). Unverified, so no rounds recorded. One profile says a $200M valuation, unverified. One source says founded 2017 with a $30,000 bank loan; the 2026 press release says launched 2016, YC page says January 2017. Function of Beauty funding detail comes from a search snippet and was not opened. Competitor evidence thin; DevaCurl predates the batch but no dated source opened. Lusbrands.com redirects to loveurcurls.com. Completeness pass: the $120K seed of 2018-03-14 rests on CB Insights and Seedtable (databases); Preqin's $1.1M figure conflicts and is not recorded. TechCrunch (2018-03-14) says the company was self-funded by the founder and gives no round amount.
